name: Ater
overview: Ater was a male member of the tribe of Levi known primarily for his descendants who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. His significance is noted in the post-exilic period as part of the restoration community. Beyond this, the biblical record provides limited additional information about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Ater appears once in Scripture and may mean 'crippled one,' 'left-handed one,' or be a variant of 'Etir.' This proper name was not given by God but reflects a personal or familial designation recorded in Ezra 2:42.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ater as a descendant of Levi, indicating his Levitical lineage. No further family details are provided beyond the mention of his sons who returned from exile.
scriptureSignificance: Ater's importance lies in his role as an ancestor of Levites who participated in the return to Judah following the captivity. This connection highlights the restoration of the Levitical priestly line and the reestablishment of worship and community life in Jerusalem. His mention in Ezra underscores the faithfulness of God's people in preserving their heritage through challenging times.
